## Learning Outcomes

Yesterday: one `.qmd` → a branded PDF. Today, the other axis: **one file to many**. You will be able to:

- **structure** several `.qmd` files into one Quarto **project** with shared configuration (`_quarto.yml`).
- **build** a navigable, **branded website** with within-page cross-references.
- make its builds **reproducible**, produce a **publishable folder**, and optionally put it online.

By the end, the same penguins data and yesterday's report will form a **website your team can
publish**.

::: notes
- **Say:** "Yesterday: one `.qmd` to a branded PDF. Today: many files, one project, then publish."
:::

## How today works

**Same shape as yesterday**: two rounds of **watch → your turn**, each ending in a
**Challenge** in the lab, with a **break** between the rounds.

The **Your turn** callout flags each switch to the lab.

::: notes
- **Say:** "Same rhythm as yesterday: watch, then you build it."
- **Schedule:** break at 15:00, resume at 15:30.
:::

# Part 1: Build and structure a project {.center}

From one file to a whole site.

## Why a *project*? {#why-project}

Quarto identifies the project root by searching **up** from the file being rendered and using the
**nearest `_quarto.yml`**.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
``` {.yaml filename="day2-projects/_quarto.yml"}
project:
  type: website
  output-dir: _site
format:
  html:
    toc: true
```
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.incremental}
- This is the nearest `_quarto.yml`, so `day2-projects/` is the project root.
- `quarto render` with no file argument builds **every** page in it.
- The `format:` settings apply to every page.
- **`output-dir`**: where the built site is written. Publish *that* folder.
:::
:::
::::

. . .

**Nearest wins.** Quarto ignores any `_quarto.yml` files above the project root.

::: notes
- **Say:** "Place `_quarto.yml` in a folder to make that folder the project root."
- **Do:** render once and show the output move from beside the `.qmd` into `_site/`.
- **Ask:** "Where is the root if a folder above also has a `_quarto.yml`?" (The nearer one.)
:::

## Directory metadata: `_metadata.yml` {#metadata}

Yesterday a header set the defaults and a cell overrode them. `_metadata.yml` applies the **same
principle** to every page in a **folder**, so you do not repeat the options in each header:

``` {.yaml filename="reports/_metadata.yml"}
# applies to every .qmd in reports/
execute:
  warning: false
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
```

The same precedence rule now applies across files: **document header** > `_metadata.yml` >
`_quarto.yml`. Set broad defaults, then override them at the document or folder level.

::: aside
`reports/` is the subfolder in today's lab. Its options apply to the two pages inside it, not to the
pages at the project root.
:::

**Learn more:** [Directory metadata](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/quarto-projects.html#directory-metadata)

::: notes
- **Say:** "Same precedence rule as yesterday, now across project, folder, page, and cell."
- **Do not re-teach:** widen the rule only.
:::

## Websites: pages and navigation {#websites .aside-flow}

`type: website` makes the folder a **site**. Define the navigation once in
`_quarto.yml`, and Quarto applies it to every page.

``` {.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
website:
  title: "Penguin Lab"
  navbar:              # list the entries yourself
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - href: analysis.qmd
        text: Analysis
  sidebar:
    contents: auto     # or let Quarto derive them
```

. . .

With `contents: auto`, Quarto builds the sidebar from the folder structure. Each page's `title:`
becomes its label, each subfolder becomes a section, and pages appear alphabetically unless they
set `order:`. New pages are included automatically.

::: {.aside}
**Listings** turn a folder of pages into an auto-generated index (a blog, a gallery of reports) via
`listing:` on a page.
:::

**Learn more:** [Websites](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/) ·
[Listings](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-listings.html)

::: notes
- **Do:** `quarto preview` and show the navigation plus the built-in search.
- **Say:** "Enumerate the navbar, derive the sidebar. Both live in one file."
- **Next:** independent pages explain the cross-reference rule.
- **Watch for:** links are relative to source files, not `_site`.
:::

## Cross-references across a project {#xrefs}

Within **one page**, `@fig-`, `@tbl-`, `@eq-` resolve to a numbered, linked reference, exactly as
on Day 1. (Section headings work the same way with `@sec-`.)

. . .

Across **different website pages**, they do **not** auto-number: a website renders each page on its
own, so link between pages with ordinary Markdown links and the **navbar/sidebar** instead:

``` markdown
See the [analysis page](analysis.qmd) for the model.
```

::: {.callout-note title="Project-wide numbering is a *book*"}
If you need "Figure 3.2" to resolve *across* chapters, that's `type: book`: Quarto renders a book as
one unit with global numbering. A **website** keeps per-page numbering.
:::

**Learn more:** [Cross-references](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/cross-references.html) ·
[Book cross-references](https://quarto.org/docs/books/book-crossrefs.html)

::: notes
- **Before session:** confirm that website pages do not resolve cross-page `@fig-` references.
- **If asked:** `@sec-` resolves without `number-sections`; the option only numbers the heading.
:::

## One brand → the whole project: `_brand.yml` {#brand}

Yesterday `_brand.yml` sat next to your report. At the **project root**, Quarto auto-discovers it for
**every page**:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}
``` {.yaml filename="_brand.yml"}
color:
  palette:
    teal: "#4C979F"
  primary: teal
typography:
  fonts:
    - family: Albert Sans
      source: google
  base:
    family: Albert Sans
```
:::
::: {.column width="46%"}
- **Every page and every deck** inherits it from that one root file, so you never name it in a page.
- Add a page later? Branded on render, nothing to wire up.
- Need an exception? `brand: false` opts a page out. `brand: other.yml` points it elsewhere.

![](../images/brand-yml-wide-color.svg){width="300px" fig-alt="Brand YAML logo: a multicolor circular icon beside the words BRAND YAML."}
:::
::::

**Learn more:** [Quarto brand](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/brand.html) ·
[brand.yml spec](https://posit-dev.github.io/brand-yml/)

::: notes
- **Say:** it styled your HTML yesterday too, not only the PDF. Yesterday's lab framed it as a Typst thing.
- **Do:** show the site before/after adding `_brand.yml`.
- **Say:** "Brand once at the project root, not once per page."
- **Do not reveal:** theme-layer order; it is the lab exercise.
- **Before session:** demo uses `[cosmo, brand]` or no named theme.
- **If asked:** plots need `theme_brand_ggplot2()`; `brand: false` opts out.
- **If asked (font changes, colors do not):** a bare `theme: cosmo` expands to `[brand, cosmo]` and
  later layers win, so cosmo's `$primary` replaces the brand color. The font arrives as
  `--bs-body-font-family`, which cosmo does not set, so it survives.
:::

## Your turn {#your-turn-1}

::: {.callout-tip title="Your turn"}
Head to the **[Lab](../../labs/quarto-projects/index.qmd#website-challenge)** and the **Website
Challenge**: turn a set of `.qmd` files into a navigable, **branded website**: `_quarto.yml`, a navbar, and
the shared brand.
:::

You can now structure files into a branded, navigable **website**. After the break we make its builds
reproducible and prepare it for publication.

::: notes
- **Say:** "Website Challenge: project, navigation, brand, folder options, then an optional listing.
  Work until the break at 15:00; we resume at 15:30."
- **Ask:** "Where did the HTML move?"
- **Ask:** "The font changed but the navbar did not. Why?"
- **Ask:** "You edited no `.qmd`; where did the option come from?"
- **Watch for:** wrong working folder; rendering one file; links aimed at `_site`.
- **Catch-up:** `solutions/day2/`.
:::

# Part 2: Scale and publish {.center}

Make builds reproducible, then prepare the project for publication.

::: notes
- **Say:** "You built the site. Now make its builds reproducible, then publish it."
- **Do:** stop `quarto preview` before the freeze exercises.
:::

## Freeze: skip unchanged computations {#freeze}

Computations can be slow: you do not want every prose edit to re-run a 20-minute model fit. Two tools
are easy to confuse:

::: {.incremental}
- **`cache`**: the **compute engine's** cache, not Quarto's. It defers to *knitr* (R) or *Jupyter Cache*.
  Per-**cell**, kept until that cell's code changes, and it works in a **single document**.
- **`freeze`**: **Quarto's** switch for when a document re-executes.
  **Project-only**: rendering one file always runs it. Results live in `_freeze/`. Once every page
  has frozen results, **CI** *(the automated build)* can rebuild those pages without R.
:::

. . .

``` {.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

With `freeze: auto`, Quarto compares the page's current source with the source recorded alongside
its stored output. If the content is unchanged, Quarto reuses the output. If it changed, Quarto
runs the code again. Re-saving an unchanged file does not trigger computation.

::: notes
- **Say:** "A prose edit should not rerun a 20-minute model."
- **Contrast:** cache = engine, per cell; freeze = Quarto, per document, project only.
- **Do:** show `_freeze/` on disk, one folder per page.
- **Payoff:** commit `_freeze/`; CI can build without R.
- **Next:** `freeze: true` gives manual control.
:::

## The `freeze: true` workflow {#freeze-workflow}

With **`freeze: true`**, a project build **reuses `_freeze/` even when the source changed**. You
refresh a page when you choose to, by rendering that one file (a single-file render always executes):

``` {.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
execute:
  freeze: true
```

``` bash
quarto render analysis.qmd     # runs the code, rewrites _freeze/ — commit it with your change
```

. . .

With `freeze: true`, the workflow is: **edit a page → render that one file → commit `_freeze/`**.
Once every page has been frozen, the project build and **CI** can reuse those results without R.
This is how **quarto.org** is built.

. . .

`freeze: auto` instead lets the *build* recompute a page whose source changed. With `true`, you
decide when to recompute each page.

::: notes
- **Say:** "With `true`, only a direct document render recomputes the page."
- **Watch for:** a page with no `_freeze/` entry and a new page still execute.
- **If a render fails** with `cannot open file '<name>.qmd'`, delete the leftover
  `<name>.knit.md` or `<name>.rmarkdown`, then render again.
- **Contrast:** `auto` recomputes changed pages; `true` requires manual refresh.
- **Example:** quarto.org uses `true` and commits `_freeze/`.
:::

## Reproducibility has two parts {#renv}

`freeze` pins the **results**. It doesn't pin **what produced them** (the package versions):

- **`freeze`** → `_freeze/`: do not repeat slow computation.
- **`renv.lock`** → *"pin the packages, so the team rebuilds the same environment."*

``` r
renv::init()       # once, to start tracking
renv::snapshot()   # write renv.lock
renv::restore()    # rebuild the same env
```

Together: a colleague (or CI) rebuilds the *same* site, with or without re-running the analysis.

**Learn more:** [renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/)

::: notes
- **Say:** "freeze pins results; `renv.lock` pins package versions."
- **Timing:** drop this first if short.
:::

## Publishing {#publishing}

Publishing has two steps: **render the project, then point a host at `output-dir`.**

``` bash
quarto render              # builds the whole project into _site/
```

- `_site/` is the whole deliverable. Point any static host at it (an internal server, your
  department's pages, a hosting service).
- **Posit Connect Cloud** takes it in one command, with a free account and **no repository**:

``` bash
quarto publish posit-connect-cloud
```

The first run opens a browser to sign in, then uploads the site.

`quarto publish` renders the project first by default. Add `--no-render` to upload the existing
`_site/`.

::: {.callout-tip title="Optional: publish your site"}
Publish your site and open it on your phone. The lab has the steps. If you skip publishing, you
still have the complete `_site/` folder.
:::

::: notes
- **Do:** run `quarto publish posit-connect-cloud` and show browser sign-in.
- **Say:** "`_site/` is the deliverable. This command puts it on a URL."
- **Say:** "`quarto publish` renders by default. Add `--no-render` to send the `_site/` folder you
  already built."
- **Mention:** free Posit account required; skipping loses nothing.
- **If asked:** scheduled and repository builds are also available.
:::

## Your turn {#your-turn-2}

::: {.callout-tip title="Your turn"}
Return to the **Reproducible Build Challenge** in the
**[Lab](../../labs/quarto-projects/index.qmd#reproducible-build-challenge)**. Make the build skip unchanged
pages, bring **yesterday's report** onto the site, then run
the guided `freeze: true` experiment. The result is a publishable `_site/` folder. Publishing
and the dashboard are optional.
:::

::: notes
- **Say:** "Minimum: freeze works and yesterday's report is a page. The `freeze: true` experiment
  completes the core."
- **Ask:** "How can you prove the code did not run?"
- **Ask:** "Where do cache and freeze write results? Which folder do you commit?"
- **Celebrate:** the Day-1 report becoming a site page.
- **Catch-up:** `solutions/day2/`; fast finishers publish, then inspect the dashboard.
:::

## Extending Quarto {#extensions}

**Extensions** add features that Quarto does not include by default: shortcodes, filters, custom
formats, and revealjs plugins.

``` bash
quarto add quarto-ext/fontawesome           # icon shortcodes
quarto use template quarto-journals/plos    # start an article in a journal format
```

They install into **`_extensions/`** next to `_quarto.yml`, so they belong to the project, not to
your machine. Commit the folder, as you do `_freeze/`, so other contributors use the same extensions
when they render the project.

**Learn more:** [Quarto extension listing](https://quarto.org/docs/extensions/) ·
[m.canouil.dev/quarto-extensions](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-extensions/) (a searchable,
community-maintained catalog)

::: notes
- **Say:** "Before you write a Lua filter, look in the listings. Someone has probably done it."
- **Do:** open the community catalog and filter by Formats.
- **Watch for:** `quarto add` must run inside the project folder.
- **If asked:** `quarto add` prompts for confirmation and installs from a GitHub repository or an
  archive URL.
:::

## What you can do now {#wrap-up}

You can now:

- structure `.qmd` files into a **project** with `_quarto.yml`, `output-dir`, and `_metadata.yml`.
- build a **branded website** with navigation and explain why cross-page references differ from a book.
- make builds **reproducible** (`freeze` + `renv.lock`) and produce a **publishable `_site/`** for a
  host or CI.
- optionally publish the site to Posit Connect Cloud.

. . .

**You've built the two axes:** one document to a branded PDF (Day 1), then one folder to a site ready
to publish (Day 2). Yesterday's report is now a page of that site.

::: notes
- **Close with:** "Yesterday's document is now a page of today's site."
:::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
